h: Make Melrose a proper half day
p: Priorwood is a garden for slowing down, and most people find somewhere between half an hour and an hour does it nicely. The good news is that it sits in the middle of one of the prettiest little towns in the Scottish Borders, so it's the perfect opening act rather than the whole show.

Start with the abbey next door. Melrose Abbey is a gorgeous red sandstone ruin looked after by Historic Environment Scotland, with carvings that reward a close look and a famous link to Robert the Bruce, whose heart is said to be buried in the grounds. Pair the two and you've got a proper history-and-gardens morning without moving the car.

Got walking legs? The Eildon Hills rise right behind the town, three distinctive peaks with sweeping views over the Tweed valley, and you can climb them straight from Melrose. St Cuthbert's Way, the long-distance path to Lindisfarne, also starts here, so even a short stretch of it makes a nice add-on. At Newstead, just east of town, you'll find the site of Trimontium, a big Roman fort named after those three hills.

A few miles west sits Abbotsford, the extraordinary home Sir Walter Scott built for himself beside the Tweed, which makes a great second stop. Rugby fans might like to know Melrose is where the sevens game was born, back in 1883. And if you don't fancy driving, the Borders Railway runs from Edinburgh to Tweedbank, a short hop from town. Bring a bag for the high street, because the independent shops are hard to walk past.
